newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S BRM CALLS NEW TENDER FOR 25,000 TNS SCRAP.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S BRM CALLS NEW TENDER FOR 25,000 TNS SCRAP.

text.p: Romania's Bucharest-based commodities exchange will call a tender to sell 25,000 tonnes of scrap iron this month, the second such offer this year, the exchange said.
The minimum starting price for a tonne of iron scrap offered in the international tender scheduled for November 28 had been set at $95, Bursa Romana de Marfuri (BRM) said in a statement.
The scrap came from old rolling stock, it said.
Bidders have until 26 November to submit offers.
Last month, the BRM held another tender for the same quantity. The 25,000 tonnes scrap on offer was bought by an Italian company at $95 a tonne, same as the starting price.
Till mid-1996, Romania applied a full ban on scrap iron exports.
But in July, the Balkan country set an export quota for scrap iron of 100,000 tonnes this year with plans to fully liberalise export of the commodity by 1998.
Scrap iron from the shipping sector and rolling stock would make the bulk of those exports, the industry ministry said.

Liberalisation of scrap iron exports is part of Romania's strategy to adapt its legislation to that of the EU internal market, in view of its possible membership. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
